# Molecular Animation

> Open-source Python framework and Blender 5.2 pipeline that turns a scientific brief and PDB/mmCIF or AlphaFold structures into honest, beautiful molecular animation of proteins, nucleic acids and ligands: scripted scenes, rendered takes, labelled and clean MP4/WebM films with posters, and a production record that tags every beat as experimental, simulation-derived or illustrative. It can be driven by an AI agent (Claude Code through Blender MCP) or by hand.

- Code: https://github.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation (Apache-2.0). Films: the GitHub releases.
- The Python package is `molanim`: a pure-numpy science layer (mmCIF and assemblies, atom-matched states, constrained morphs, pathway profiles, membranes, ion transits, thermal motion, cartoons, electrostatics) and a Blender layer (`molanim.blender`). The command line is `pipeline.py`: new, pdb, build, still, preview, render, deliver, motion, check, lint.
- Motion is modelled, not simulated: tumbling and diffusion at hydrodynamic rates, elastic-network normal modes and side-chain turns at literature rates. It is not molecular dynamics.
- Requirements: Blender 5.2, a Cycles-capable GPU, ffmpeg, Python 3.10+. Tested on Windows 11.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/README.md): overview, quick start, FAQ, comparison with Molecular Nodes, PyMOL, ChimeraX and VMD
- [Workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/docs/workflow.md): how a brief becomes a delivered film
- [Principles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/docs/principles.md): what makes the films good and honest
- [Framework API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/docs/framework.md): the `molanim` modules and the pipeline tools
- [Motion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/docs/motion.md): how molecules move, with rates and sources
- [Depiction sources](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/docs/depiction-sources.md): the physics behind cartoons, Coulombic colouring and pi lobes
- [Setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/docs/setup.md): Blender, GPU, ffmpeg and Blender MCP
- [Blender 5.x notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/docs/blender-5.md): the Blender 5.2 Python API, what coding models trained on older Blender write instead, and how the repo checks it (an API probe and a lint)
- [Agent guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/AGENTS.md): operating rules for coding agents working in the repo

## Examples

- [Channelrhodopsin case study](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/examples/channelrhodopsin/README.md): a 21 s film for the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, from brief to delivery (PDB 9GO1/9GO2)
- [ART film record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/projects/art-rna/record.md): an RNA-making reverse transcriptase locus of phage SA1, with AlphaFold Server predictions
- [Website plates record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmadeusBio-ai/Molecular_Animation/main/projects/website/record.md): stills and loops from PDB and AlphaFold DB structures
